name: AKU nursing programme invited to East Africa

content.text: Honourable Musyoka had arrived in Pakistan on February 15, at tile invitation of the Aga Khan University (AKU) to continue dialogue regarding tile University's proposed programme for Advanced Nursing Studies in East Africa. He was accompanied by senior officials from tile Kenyan health and education ministries including Professor Justin Irina, Secretary, and Commission for Higher Education, Professor Julius Samson Meme, Director of Medical Services, Ministry of Health and Ms. Margaret Kaseje, Regional Health Program Officer, Aga Khan Foundation, Kenya.

Setting up of such a programme had been requested by the East African nursing leadership as well as public and private health officials in order to improve the quality of patient care provided throughout tile region. The Programme would offer continuing education for nurses in practice, research, administration and higher education in several cities of East Africa. In discussions about tile Progranune, Honourable Musyoka said that besides leading to improved nursing practices and healthcare delivery, it reflected the need for greater South to South collaboration.

AKU occupies a pivotal position in tile social development activities of tile Aga Khan Development Network (AKDN). which comprises a group of institutions working to improve living conditions and opporturIities in specific regions of the developing world. The proposed nursing Programme in East Africa would also fulfill AKU's mandate as an international University which seeks to serve multiple constituencies through tile diffusion of its intellectual products. When this progranune is implemented, "We," said Dr Shamsh Kassim-Lakha, President of tile Aga Khan University. "will be the first university in Pakistan to have an overseas campus."

During their week-long stay, tile delegates held meetings with tile Governor of Sindh, Lt. General (Retd.) Moinuddin Haider as well as Federal Ministers of Education and Foreign Affairs and other senior Govenunent officials. Discussions focused on the status of tile proposed Nursing programme in East Africa and of health and education in Pakistan, as well as social development issues of mutual relevance.

On his visit to Aga Khan University School of Nursing (AKUSON), Honourable Musyoka praised tile innovative working and leaming environment of the School and considered it an example for similar institutions throughout tile developing world, Professor Meme, tile Kenyan Health Ministry's Director of Medical Services said with institutions like AKUSON nursing in tile South could enter the new millenium 'with a spring ... not a crawl.'

The AKU Institute for Educational Development focuses on tile professional development of teachers and promoting leadership in education. While visiting AKU-IED, the Minister expressed an interest in tile possible expansion of its activities in East Africa and commended tile Institute's efforts in teacher education and school improvement. The more than two dozen East African course participants described tile attitudinal transformation they had experienced at AKU-IED and how it had enabled tllem to reconceptualize their roles as teachers and teacher educators.

On a visit to Sulranabad, one of Karachi 's squatter settlements (katchi abadis), where AKU participates in various community-based initiatives for education and social uplift, Honourable Musyoka observed, "This was an excellent example of a university's role in promoting the health of the community."

The Kenyan delegation also travelled to the Northern Areas to familiarize themselves with the activities and projects of AKDN in the fields of health, education and rural development in these under-served, rural parts of Pakistan. During visits to Gilgit, Punyal and Hunza divisions, the delegation met officials of the Government and the AKDN, and noted that these programmes provided good examples of the collaboration between the Government and the NGO sector for the upliftment of the people at the grassroots level.

content.description: "We would like to transplant this excellent institution into Kenya," said the Honourable Stephen Kalonzo Musyoka, Minister for Education and Human Resource Development, Government of Kenya, while addressing a group of fifteen Kenyan nurses and medical students currently studying at tile Aga Khan University.
